reviewers.codex: completed (8 findings — landed late after initial empty read)
reviewers.copilot: completed (3 findings — landed late after initial progress-only read)

convergenceNote: All three reviewers were run in parallel (autonomous mode). Codex and Copilot output files initially read empty/progress-only and were re-read on their late completion notifications; both produced substantive High-severity findings that materially refined the plan from a binary fail-closed (pidAlive:false) design to a tri-state (true/false/null) design. Findings applied directly to draft-plan.md + stories-outline.md + suggested-decomposition.json rather than via review-loop.mjs (whose planning-engine relies on the same codex-exec path that showed Windows flakiness this run).

findings.description: Non-Windows fail-closed path was a behavior change with no explicit acceptance criterion.
findings.resolution: Added AC9 (non-Windows tri-state) and flagged the behavior change in Technical Constraints; the converged non-Windows behavior is unverifiable-live -> null (Windows-scoped guarantee).

findings.description: AC1-AC3 under-specified the exact injected-seam inputs/outputs (esp. the EPERM/null split).
findings.resolution: Rewrote AC1-AC3 with concrete seam inputs (foreign image vs non-matching pwsh cmdline; matching launcher-script basename; describeProcess->null vs foreign-image split).

findings.description: Non-Windows pseudocode returned true on a bare isProcessAlive==true, which can report a recycled PID as alive — contradicting the never-false-positive contract. Either fail-closed on non-Windows or scope the guarantee to Windows.
findings.resolution: Converged design maps non-Windows unverifiable-live -> null (never a verified alive); guarantee explicitly Windows-scoped. AC9 pins it.

findings.description: tests/integration/list-members-health.test.js:49-55 writes a real node.exe PID to alivemember's launcher.pid and asserts state==='alive'; the verifier rejects non-pwsh images, so this integration test breaks and was not in the plan's test scope.
findings.resolution: Added the integration test to Files-to-Modify and AC12: alivemember fixture becomes a genuine verified pwsh launcher (matching launcher.pid.scriptPath).

findings.description: Existing health.test.js alive/quiet/shape fixtures (lines 70-83, 133-175) rely on PID 111 being alive via process.kill stub; the new default path calls real describeProcess(111) and they will fail unless migrated to inject seams.
findings.resolution: Added AC11 requiring migration of those fixtures to inject a matching describeProcess seam.

findings.description: Release-surface stamp count inconsistent ('7 stamps' vs '6 stamps + version test').
findings.resolution: Standardized to '6 version-bearing files + tests/version.test.js' in plan, stories, and research-brief.

findings.description: Parallel handoff line is unnecessary for a single serial cluster.
findings.resolution: Next Step uses the serial handoff; Suggested Decomposition keeps the parallel line (skill-required) but notes serial is the recommended path.

findings.description: AC10 (whole-suite green) omitted the integration test that would break.
findings.resolution: Added explicit AC12 (integration) + AC13 (crash-sweep audit); AC14 keeps the whole-suite gate.

findings.description: Fail-closing an unverifiable (describeProcess===null) PID to pidAlive:false -> state dead would route FALSE member-crashed notifications (v3.13 crash sweep, member-crash-notifications.js:292 fires on state==='dead'), violating the crash-sweep invariant for a transiently-unverifiable but genuinely-alive member.
findings.resolution: Core design change: unverifiable (CIM-null / non-Windows) -> null (NOT false). deriveHealthState then yields unknown for fresh-heartbeat members, which the crash sweep skips. Only definitive disconfirmation (ESRCH / verified-foreign) -> false -> dead. Added AC3/AC4/AC5 to pin no-false-crash + sweep-eligible-when-verified-foreign.

findings.description: Test scope missed tests/member-crash-notifications.test.js PID-stubbed-alive fixtures that expect the sweep to skip; under verification they become non-pwsh -> dead/foreign unless updated.
findings.resolution: Added the crash-notifications test to Files-to-Modify and AC13 (audit + update).

findings.description: AC3 didn't distinguish 'verified not this launcher' (definitive dead) from 'temporarily unverifiable' (CIM-null), given the crash-notification coupling.
findings.resolution: Split into AC3 (CIM-null -> null/unknown) and AC5 (verified-foreign -> false/dead, sweep-eligible); the tri-state design encodes the distinction.
